title: Every CLI process and hook pays 1.5-5 s cold start because native tree-sitter addons load at module import
observation: loadNativeTreeSitter() is called at module top level in src/extractors/parse.ts:21 and src/constitution/g2BehaviorCandidates.ts:182. It copies six native .node addons into a fresh per-process temp dir and requires the copies, so every process that merely imports the CLI module graph (hunch --version, every Claude Code hook event) pays the copy plus a dlopen of never-before-seen binaries. The earlier belief that npx was the cost was wrong: npx vs direct node on the cached dist measured the same range. RESOLVED 2026-09-20: PR #366 (merge a9119807; fix ff017fad 'load the native tree-sitter addons on first parse, not at import', plus 23a3f1f0 so a native parser load failure aborts the run instead of wiping the graph) shipped in 1.40.0; test/cold-start.test.ts guards it.
evidence: 2026-09-20, macOS, Node 22.23.1, dist 1.39.3, /usr/bin/time -p x5: node -e 0 median 0.04 s; node dist/cli/index.js --version min 1.66 s median 3.26 s; PreToolUse hook min 2.34 s median 4.89 s; UserPromptSubmit median 4.58 s; Stop median 8.32 s (noisy machine)
node --cpu-prof: dlopen = 98.3% of sampled time on --version, 89.7% on the pre-edit hook

fresh-process await import(): dist/extractors/parse.js 4797 ms, dist/extractors/indexer.js 3701 ms, dist/mcp/server.js 2197 ms; commander 11 ms, zod 23 ms, node:sqlite 0.3 ms, each tree-sitter grammar package imported directly 5-11 ms
2026-09-19 sessions: hook wall time totalled about 37 minutes
